topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview on cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the learning outcomes, the multi-step mutation progression model, and the framework of cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Deregulation of growth factor and proliferation signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic and tumor suppressor mutations in cell-surface receptors and downstream cascades drive autonomous proliferation and cell survival.

topics.label: Differentiation block in hematopoietic and epithelial cancers
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how genetic disruptions prevent cancer cells from completing terminal differentiation across leukemias and colorectal carcinoma.

topics.label: Evasion of apoptosis, replicative immortality, and cellular stress controls
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms cells use to bypass programmed cell death and replicative limits through p53 regulation, telomere maintenance, and senescence evasion.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how cancer cells alter their metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, metabolic rewiring, and metabolic gene mutations.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how tumors activate the angiogenic switch to recruit new blood vessels required for nutrient perfusion and continued growth.

topics.label: Mechanisms, inefficiency, and genomics of cancer metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the multi-step metastatic cascade, the seed-and-soil hypothesis, and genomic characteristics associated with metastatic dissemination.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer provides concluding remarks on cancer hallmark convergence, recommends further reading, and closes the session.
